history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row seq 2340 duplicates the already-researched record = seq 1052 (id chaturdasha-devata-temple-old-agartala); no separate shrine exists under this CSV name. Built by Maharaja Krishna Kishore Manikya (r. 1760–1783) at Old Agartala (Puratani Haveli/Khayerpur) after the capital was shifted from Udaipur — following conflicts with Shamsher Gazi — and the fourteen deities were moved with it; an earlier temple stood at Udaipur. The Chaturdasha Devata are the patron gods of the Tripura royal family: only their heads (busts) are enshrined, in a blend of tribal (Kokborok) and Puranic worship; only Shiva, Uma and Vishnu are worshipped daily. CSV town 'Sabroom' is WRONG — corrected to Old Agartala (Khayerpur), West Tripura. Note: sources differ on when the capital moved again to present-day Agartala (1840 vs 1870); flag.

name: Chaturdasha Devata Temple (Fourteen Gods Temple)
town_description: Old Agartala (Khayerpur/Puratani Haveli) was the former capital of Tripura under the Manikya kings, about 6–14 km from present-day Agartala. It is best known for the Chaturdasha Devata Temple and the week-long Kharchi Puja fair held there every July.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~20 km)
travel.road: Old Agartala/Khayerpur road; ~6–14 km from Agartala city centre

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; July for the Kharchi Puja festival week
